roles: Full stack and mobile: NestJS, Next.js, React Native, PostgreSQL
summary: I build and run software that moves money, and I do the security work on it myself: threat models, hardening, testing, incident response. Trained in information security first (BSc, 2019 to 2023), learned full-stack and mobile development by shipping. Founder of Devsirch Hub in Nairobi, where the same person who writes the code is accountable for keeping it safe in production.
aside: Almost all of my work is in private client repositories, so the public repos here are not representative. The activity card includes the private ones.

practices.label: Money paths
practices.detail: Integer amounts only. Every balance change runs in a database transaction with the row locked. Transaction state machines are enforced by Postgres triggers, so an application bug cannot move a payment backwards. Every payment mutation carries an idempotency key that is claimed before the provider call, not after.

practices.label: Bank and provider integrations
practices.detail: The service that talks to a bank is the only service that talks to a bank. Webhooks are logged raw before they are parsed, deduplicated under a lock, and never trusted on their own: the provider's status API confirms them. Callback URLs are set by the server, never accepted from a caller.

practices.label: Data at rest
practices.detail: National IDs, bank account numbers and provider credentials are AES-256-GCM encrypted per row, with the row's identity bound into the authenticated data so a ciphertext cannot be moved between rows. Audit logs are append-only and hash-chained. Personal data is redacted at the logger, not by whoever remembers to.

practices.label: Access
practices.detail: Ownership is checked in the handler and again by row-level security. Services authenticate to each other with short-lived Ed25519 tokens. Admin actions need a second factor; the sensitive ones need it again. Secrets are read from a secret manager and the service refuses to boot if one is missing.

practices.label: Mobile
practices.detail: Tokens in the platform keystore, never in app storage. Public-key pinning. Device attestation checked on the server before any payout. Screens that show a PIN or confirm a payment block screenshots.

practices.label: Operations
practices.detail: Metrics, traces and logs through one collector. Every alert has a severity, a destination and a runbook. A webhook that fails signature verification is treated as an attack, and a ledger that disagrees with the bank is an incident.

practices.label: Testing my own work
practices.detail: OWASP API Security Top 10 and MASVS reviews before launch, with findings tracked until the fix is merged and retested. I say plainly that this is self-review, and that an independent test is a different thing.

workflow.label: Design first
workflow.detail: The design is agreed in writing before code. Anything it did not settle is written into the PR as an assumption, so it can be argued with.

workflow.label: Review before merge
workflow.detail: Every change is reviewed before it merges, and the findings are listed in full before anything is filtered out.

workflow.label: Incidents become checks
workflow.detail: After an incident I write down the lesson with the date, and where a script can enforce it, it becomes a CI gate.

workflow.label: Real devices
workflow.detail: A mobile change is tested on a physical phone before it ships, including a cheap one.

projects.name: ChallengeMe
projects.tagline: Side-competitions platform for golf clubs in Kenya.
projects.detail: Players pay entry fees by M-Pesa, club admins run events and payouts from a live dashboard. Payment webhooks are idempotent and confirmed against the provider before anything is credited, and a club's wallet is checked before any payout.

projects.name: RSA Boda
projects.tagline: Savings group platform for boda-boda riders in Kenya, built for BladeDoc Network.
projects.detail: Three mobile apps, an admin dashboard, a backend and a separate payments service with direct bank integration for collections, payouts and reconciliation. Members save, borrow and fund group projects; officials approve payouts under dual control. Entering Google Play review, November 2026.

learning: Offensive work on TryHackMe and Hack The Box, Burp Suite against my own apps first.
Mobile security: MASVS and MASTG, applied to the React Native apps I ship.
